title: “Monks, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades, and ceases, monks, devas and humans dwell in suffering. They…
content: “Monks, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades, and ceases, monks, devas and humans dwell in suffering. They delight in sound … in odor … in taste … in touch … Monks, devas and humans delight in phenomena, are excited by phenomena. When phenomena change, fade, and cease, monks, devas and humans dwell in suffering. Monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having directly known as they actually are the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, does not delight in form, does not cherish form, is not excited by form. When form changes, fades, and ceases, monks, the Tathāgata dwells at ease. He does not delight in sound … in odor … in taste … in touch … Having directly known as they actually are the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to phenomena, the Tathāgata does not delight in phenomena, does not cherish them, is not excited by them. When phenomena change, fade, and cease, the Tathāgata dwells at ease.”

title: “Monks, there are these five dangers for one who is mindless, not clearly comprehending, and falls asleep. What five? He sleeps badly; he wakes up…
content: “Monks, there are these five dangers for one who is mindless, not clearly comprehending, and falls asleep. What five? He sleeps badly; he wakes up badly; he has bad dreams; devas do not protect him; impure things flow out, nocturnal emission. These, monks, are the five dangers for one who is mindless, not clearly comprehending, and falls asleep. Monks, there are these five benefits for one who is mindful, clearly comprehending, and falls asleep. What five? He sleeps well; he wakes up well; he has no bad dreams; devas protect him; impure things do not flow out. These, monks, are the five benefits for one who is mindful, clearly comprehending, and falls asleep.”

title: Elder Kappa: Full of various impurities, Where there is no purity — Like a long-stagnant puddle, A great boil, a wound. Full of blood and…
content:
Elder Kappa:

Full of various impurities,
Where there is no purity —
Like a long-stagnant puddle,
A great boil, a wound.

Full of blood and pus,
Sunk in a pit of filth —
This body oozes fluid,
Constantly oozing impurity.

Bound by sixty sinews,
Plastered with flesh as mortar,
Clad in skin as armor —
This foul body is useless.

Connected by a chain of bones,
Tied together with sinews —
By their combined power,
They create various postures.

Always heading toward death,
Approaching the end of life —
There, abandoned,
People go according to their desire.

The body, shrouded by ignorance,
Bound by four bonds,
Sinks in the flood,
Caught in the net of underlying tendencies —

Fettered by five hindrances,
Obsessed by thought,
Following the root of craving,
Covered by the veil of delusion.

Thus this body wanders,
Led by the chariot of kamma —
Sometimes success, sometimes failure —
Enduring many births of craving.

One who thinks ‘this body is mine’
Is a foolish worldling,
Increasing the fearful cemetery,
Clinging tightly to renewed existence.

One who avoids this body
As one avoids a snake smeared with feces —
That one abandons the root of existence
And attains Nibbāna, free from defilements.

title: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment.…
content: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. Udāyi, I say: ‘This person is not bound, not fettered.’ Why is that? Udāyi, the difference in his faculties has been fully understood by me.”

title: “Here, good sirs, greed is an unwholesome state, and ill-will is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons…
content: “Here, good sirs, greed is an unwholesome state, and ill-will is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons ill-will, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna. And what, good sirs, is that Middle Way that gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, leads to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration. This, good sirs, is the Middle Way that gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, leads to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.”

title: “Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world,…
content: “Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world, beings become lustful for the world. If there were no peril in the world, beings would not become disenchanted with the world. But because there is peril in the world, beings become disenchanted with the world. If there were no escape from the world, beings would not escape from the world. But because there is escape from the world, beings escape from the world.”

title: Another Elder Nun Dhīrā: Dhīrā, be steadfast, Hold fast to wholesome states. O nun, with faculties developed, Bear this last body, Having conquered the forces…
content:
Another Elder Nun Dhīrā:

Dhīrā, be steadfast,
Hold fast to wholesome states.
O nun, with faculties developed,
Bear this last body,
Having conquered the forces of Māra’s army,
Having conquered Māra with his army.

title: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained…
content: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. These six sense bases, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness.”

title: “Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body,…
content:
“Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body, speech, and mind in this life is a refuge, a cave, an island (or a lamp), a shelter, and a destination for one who has gone to death.

When a house is on fire,
The goods that are removed
Are useful to the owners,
Not those burned inside.
So too, the world is burning
With aging and death on fire —
Save yourself by giving,
For what is given is well-saved.
Here, restraint of body,
Restraint of speech and mind —
One who does this, even while dying,
Experiences happiness,
Because while still alive,
He has made merit.”

title: “One who avoids sensual desires As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head — That mindful one transcends This attachment in the world. Whoever is greedy…
content:
“One who avoids sensual desires
As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one transcends
This attachment in the world.

Whoever is greedy for sensual pleasures —
Land, gold, cows, horses,
Servants, attendants, women, relatives —

Weak, overcome by sensual pleasures,
Calamity crushes him,
Suffering follows him
As water rushes into a broken boat.

Therefore, always mindful,
One should abandon sensual pleasures.
Having abandoned them, one crosses the flood,
Having bailed out the boat, one reaches the far shore.”
